Roger Tinkoff (rogt@slip.net) wrote:

: In the book "In the Absence of the Sacred" by Jerry Mander, Mander
: makes a similar point.  Lets say that some "fringe" organization can
: somehow scrape together the money to purchase one 15-second spot on
: say, NBC during prime-time, whose message presents an alternative to
: living in techno-industrial society.  Even if they can manage this,
: any of these huge multi-national corporations can *easily* purchase
: the slot right after the "fringe" ad, as well as two more slots per
: evening for the next week, and present a much nicer, slicker-looking
: ad which debunks the "fringe" message.

You can also point out the example of "Adbusters", who tried to get a
30-second commerical aired by CBC (I think), which condemned the use of
the automobile. The CBC refused to air the advertisement. (The CBC is
Canada's public-funded TV network).

Truth is, the networks will not participate in their own destruction.
Anything remotely FC-ish qualifies. The monster's only reason is to
perpetuate itself. 'Course, now the Internet is starting to permanently
lure people away from television, and that'd be great for diversity of
thought if only there wasn't such a terrible signal-to-noise ratio.

: For what it's worth, it's hard to find any person who has not at least
: heard of the unifesto, and I'm sure plenty of people went out on the
: internet and read it just because of that.

And I bet very few people read more than a few paragraphs. Took me over a
year to get around to it, and I was sympathetic. And I doubt enough people
had the background necessary to really digest it and find it meaningful,
especially since it's written by someone who also happened to have sent
letter bombs around the USA for a few decades.

Heck, just look around here in alt.fan.unabomber. Don't see much FC
support, do you. The vast majority of people are conditioned to view ANY
serious socio-political discussion with a combination of impatience and
disgust -- same way that teenage kids view Wagnerian opera. 99.999% of the
people who've heard of "the unifesto" think of it as something written by
some "rambling psychopathic crank". I bet most don't even know its real
title.

: None of this would be possible without a system that supports:
: - The necessary knowledge and surgical equipment required to tie your
: tubes.
: - Companies to manufacture espresso machines.
: - Companies who import coffee grown in other countries.

Of course, you've gotta remember the people IN those countries who have to
grow the coffee too. It's kinda telling that one would mention
"knowledge", "equipment" and "companies", but forget that there's a whole
continent full of peasant farmers who have to grow the coffee, and who
have to be controlled by (in some cases) US-funded fascist dictatorships 
in order for the "machine" to continue to function.

: No, but any major network which decided to devote it's resources to
: presenting truly "enlightened" topics to it's viewers, regardless of
: the opinions of their corporate sponsors, would soon go broke.

Or privatized out of existence by neo-conservatives, in the case of PBS in
the USA, or TVO & CBC in Canada.
